prompt: Merchant can open a clean admin dashboard to view revenue, average order value, top products, and repeat customer rate at a glance.

intent.desiredOutcome: Merchant can open a clean admin dashboard to view revenue, average order value, top products, and repeat customer rate at a glance.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version of this app calculates metrics accurately from Shopify order data, handles edge cases like refunds or cancelled orders correctly, and displays the dashboard without lag. The UI should be clean and scannable — four key numbers at the top, the top products list below. Avoid over-design; prioritize clarity. Common pitfall: calculating repeat customers only from visible orders if pagination is needed; ensure the calculation covers your entire order history reliably.

plan.dataFlow: Once per hour the scheduled job calls acquire-job-lock to atomically test-and-set dashboard_snapshot.job_running for the merchant's row. If the lock is already held the tick aborts immediately. Otherwise the job paginates through every page of non-cancelled, non-refunded orders from Shopify, then computes total revenue, AOV, repeat-customer count, total-customer count, and top products by revenue from the full set. The resulting metrics are atomically written into the dashboard snapshot and top product snapshot rows for the merchant (replacing any prior values) and job_running is cleared as part of that write. If the fetch or compute step throws, release-job-lock clears job_running without touching the previously stored metric values so the previous snapshot survives. When the merchant opens the admin panel, the front-end calls the dashboard GET endpoint, which reads directly from the pre-computed snapshot rows and returns them instantly without touching Shopify; the front-end derives the repeat-customer rate locally from repeat_customer_count divided by total_customer_count.

triggers.jobPurpose: Recompute all dashboard metrics from the full order history and refresh the persisted snapshot.
triggers.perTickWork: The job fetches all eligible orders from Shopify, computes the four key metrics, and atomically upserts the dashboard snapshot and top product snapshot rows for the merchant, replacing the previous values.

capabilities.description: Retrieve all non-cancelled, non-refunded orders for the store including customer identity and line item revenue. The implementation must follow Shopify's cursor-based pagination (pageInfo.hasNextPage / endCursor on the orders connection) until no further page is returned, accumulating the full set in memory before any metric is computed; without exhausting pagination repeat-customer rate is silently understated.
Sum net order totals across all eligible orders to produce total revenue.

Divide total revenue by eligible order count to produce average order value. When the eligible order count is zero (new merchant or every order refunded), the computed value must be recorded as zero rather than producing a divide-by-zero error or null.
Rank products by total revenue contribution across all eligible orders.

Return both the repeat-customer count (customers with more than one eligible order) and the total-customer count (distinct customers with at least one eligible order) across the full order history; the rate itself is derived client-side from the two counts so the API response stays strictly typed and the front-end controls precision. Guest orders without a customer identifier are excluded from both counts.
Read the latest pre-computed metric snapshot for the merchant to serve the admin dashboard.
Persist the newly computed summary metrics into the dashboard snapshot row for the merchant; also clears job_running to false on successful completion.

Atomically check the dashboard_snapshot.job_running flag and set it to true only if it was false, returning whether the lock was acquired. Called at the start of each hourly tick so an in-flight predecessor can be detected and the duplicate tick aborted before any read or write begins.

Clear the dashboard_snapshot.job_running flag without modifying the previously stored metric values. Called when the hourly job aborts mid-pagination or compute, so a transient failure does not leave the lock stuck on and block all future ticks.
Persist the ranked product list into the top product snapshot rows for the merchant, replacing any prior entries.

persistence.name: dashboard_snapshot
persistence.purpose: Stores the most recently computed summary metrics for each merchant so the admin panel can load instantly.

columns.name: shop_domain
columns.purpose: identifies which merchant installation this snapshot belongs to

columns.name: repeat_customer_count
columns.purpose: Distinct customers with more than one eligible order across the full order history; numerator of the repeat-customer rate

columns.name: total_customer_count
columns.purpose: Distinct customers with at least one eligible order; denominator of the repeat-customer rate

columns.name: job_running
columns.purpose: Set true at the start of an hourly recompute and false on completion or abort; the next scheduled tick reads this flag to detect a still-running predecessor and abort rather than racing on the snapshot writes

persistence.keyedBy: one row per merchant installation, keyed by shop domain — upserted on each job run
queryPatterns: single row lookup by shop domain to serve the admin dashboard

persistence.name: top_product_snapshot
persistence.purpose: Stores the ranked list of top products by revenue for each merchant, refreshed on every job run.

columns.name: shop_domain
columns.purpose: identifies which merchant installation these product rows belong to

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the product in the external catalog

persistence.keyedBy: one row per product per merchant installation, keyed by shop domain and product external identifier — fully replaced on each job run
queryPatterns: all rows for a given shop domain ordered by rank position ascending

externalContracts.purpose: Return all pre-computed dashboard metrics and the ranked top products list for display in the admin panel. Returns repeat_customer_count and total_customer_count as separate integers (the front-end derives the rate as count/total) so the response stays strictly typed; returns top_products bounded by the limit query parameter (default 10, max 50) with top_products_count for client-side awareness of truncation.

edgeCases: An order that was later fully refunded must be excluded from all metric computations so it does not inflate revenue or order counts.
If the full order history spans multiple pages of API results, all pages must be fetched before any metric is computed to prevent understating repeat customer rate.
A customer who placed orders under multiple identifiers (guest then account) must not be double-counted as a repeat customer if they cannot be resolved to a single identity.

If the snapshot table contains no row for a merchant — such as during the window between app installation and the first completed job run — the dashboard GET must return a zeroed seed row rather than an error; this seed row must be written immediately at install time.

If the hourly job is still running when the next scheduled tick arrives, the new instance calls acquire-job-lock, which atomically reads dashboard_snapshot.job_running and only sets it true if it was false; when the lock is already held the new tick aborts immediately without reading orders or writing rows, preventing two concurrent computations from interleaving writes to the same snapshot rows.

If Shopify returns a partial or error response during order pagination, the job must invoke release-job-lock to clear job_running and abort, retaining the previous snapshot rather than overwriting it with incomplete data; without this explicit release the lock would stay held forever and block all future ticks.

If the eligible order count is zero — a brand-new merchant or one whose entire history was refunded — total_revenue, average_order_value, repeat_customer_count, and total_customer_count must all be written as zero so the dashboard renders an empty-state rather than null fields or a divide-by-zero error in compute-aov.

hld_v_findings.issue: Neither snapshot table contains a shop or tenant identifier column. Shopify apps are multi-tenant; with the current schema every merchant installation overwrites the same rows, causing cross-merchant data corruption and information leakage.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a non-nullable `shop_domain` (or `shop_id`) column to both tables, include it in the keyedBy definition, and make all query patterns and capability dataNeeds filter by it.

hld_v_findings.issue: `top_products` is typed as a bare list with no count field and the requestShape declares no limit or page parameter, violating the requirement that GET routes returning a list must expose pagination controls.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a `top_products_count` integer field to responseShape and a `limit` query parameter to requestShape (e.g., default 10, max 50) so callers can control and reason about list size.

hld_v_findings.issue: No edge case addresses overlapping job executions: if the hourly job takes longer than 60 minutes (large order history) a second instance starts and both attempt to atomically replace the same snapshot rows simultaneously, risking partial or interleaved writes.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an edge case specifying that the scheduler must acquire a distributed lock (or a job-running flag in the DB) before beginning a run and abort if the lock is already held, ensuring only one computation runs at a time.

hld_v_findings.issue: dataNeeds lists "snapshot row" and "top product rows" — table-level aliases rather than individual column names — making it impossible for LLD to derive which fields are read and verify column coverage against the persistence definitions.
hld_v_findings.fix: Replace with explicit field names from both tables (e.g., `total_revenue`, `average_order_value`, `repeat_customer_rate`, `computed_at`, `product_external_id`, `rank_position`, etc.).

hld_v_findings.issue: The edge case for an empty snapshot covers the zero-orders scenario but not the window between app installation and the first scheduled job completion, during which the snapshot table has no row at all and the admin GET has nothing to return.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an edge case stating that on first install a seed row of zeroes must be written immediately (e.g., at OAuth callback or app install webhook) so the admin panel never encounters a missing snapshot.
